title: Foods do not defile; violated women are not guilty
english: Foods do not trouble us, holy pope, if the captives ate what their masters placed before them—especially since everyone agrees that the barbarians who overran our regions did not sacrifice to idols. The apostle says, “Foods are for the belly, and the belly for foods, and God will abolish both this and those” (1 Corinthians 6:13). And the Savior, who cleanses all foods, says, “It is not what enters that defiles a person, but what comes out” (Matthew 15:11). And as for the captive women being corrupted, with the barbarians committing violation against their bodies: But if a woman’s life had already been condemned before, because she walked after the eyes of fornicators, as it is written, then clearly her immoral disposition is suspect even in the time of captivity, and such women should not readily share in the prayers. If, however, a woman who had lived in extreme chastity and had shown her former life to be clean and beyond all suspicion has now fallen into violation through force and necessity, we have the example in Deuteronomy concerning the young woman whom a man found in the open country and, after forcing her, slept with her: “You shall do nothing to the young woman; there is no capital sin for the young woman, because just as if a man rises up against his neighbor and takes his life, so is this matter. The young woman cried out, and there was no one to help her” (Deuteronomy 22:25–27). These things, then, are so.

added_allusions.reason: Foods for the belly; God will abolish both

translator_notes: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR.
This section covers Canon I; Canons II–XI follow in sections 2–11.
orientation: Gregory is writing to a bishop about how to treat Christians who were taken captive by barbarian invaders and ate food placed before them, and about women who suffered sexual violation at the hands of the barbarians.

title: Greed in the Raid Is Excommunicable
english: Greed is terrible, and there is no way to set out the divine scriptures in a single letter. In them, not only robbery is denounced as something to be avoided and dreadful, but greed in general and laying hands on what belongs to others for shameful profit are condemned, and every such person is excommunicated from the Church of God. That during the raid, amid so much wailing and lamentation, some dared to regard the very moment bringing ruin on everyone as their own opportunity for gain, is the act of impious and God-hating people who have no measure of monstrosity. Therefore it seemed right to excommunicate all such persons, lest the anger of God come upon the whole people and fall first upon the leaders who do not seek them out. For I fear, as the Scripture says, lest the impious destroy the just along with himself; for sexual immorality and greed, he says, are the things because of which the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience (Ephesians 5:6). Do not become partners with them; for you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord (Ephesians 5:7–8). Walk as children of light, for the fruit of light is found in all goodness and righteousness and truth (Ephesians 5:9), testing what is well-pleasing to the Lord (Ephesians 5:10), and do not take part in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them (Ephesians 5:11). For it is shameful even to speak of the things done by them in secret, but everything exposed by the light becomes visible (Ephesians 5:12–13). Such are the words of the apostle. If, then, while paying the penalty for their former greed, the greed they practiced in peacetime, some turn again to greed even in the very moment of wrath, profiting from the blood and destruction of men who have been uprooted — whether taken captive or murdered — what else should we expect but that they are contending alongside greed, heaping up wrath upon themselves and upon the whole people?

added_allusions.reason: μὴ συναπολέσῃ ἀσεβὴς τὸν δίκαιον, introduced by 'as the Scripture says'; Gregory adapts the LXX (Abraham asks God not to destroy the righteous with the impious)
πορνεία ... πλεονεξία, δι᾿ ἃ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας
ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας
Μὴ οὖν γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν ... φανεροῦται, quoted almost word for word

translator_notes: Rubric of the canon collection left out (editorial, not Gregory's). ἐκκήρυκτος / ἐκκηρύξαι rendered 'cast out of' and 'excommunicate'; πάντα taken adverbially ('altogether'). οὐδὲ ὑπερβολὴν ἀτοπίας ἐχόντων read as 'whose outrage leaves no room for anything worse' and rendered 'whose outrageousness nothing could surpass'. Genesis 18:23 cited because Gregory introduces the line with 'as the Scripture says', but his wording adapts the LXX (there Abraham asks God not to destroy the righteous with the impious; here the impious man brings the righteous down with him); the English follows Gregory's wording. 'Fornication ... disobedience' blends Colossians 3:5–6 (δι᾿ ἃ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργή) with Ephesians 5:3, 6; the rest quotes Ephesians 5:7–13 almost word for word. ἐπισωρεῦσαι ὀργήν may echo Romans 2:5 (θησαυρίζεις ὀργήν), but the verb differs; possible only, not cited. ἐπαγωνιζομένους τῇ πλεονεξίᾳ rendered 'pressing on still harder in their greed'. Accent θεία → θεῖα follows the source note; no change of sense.
orientation: Gregory turns from the captive women to condemn members of his own flock who exploited the raid for profit; he warns that such greed draws God's wrath on the whole church unless the offenders are cut off.

title: Warning against profiteering from the suffering of fellow believers
english: Consider Achan son of Zerah: he sinned by sinning against the devoted thing, and wrath came upon the whole assembly of Israel. He alone sinned, yet he did not die alone in his sin. For us, any gain that is not ours but belongs to another at this time ought to be considered a devoted thing. That Achan took from the spoil of the enemies; these people now take from the spoil of brothers, gaining destructive profit.

Inline Joshua 22:20

added_allusions.reason: Οὐκ ἰδοὺ Ἄχαρ ὁ τοῦ Ζαρᾶ ... μὴ μόνος ἀπέθανεν, LXX almost word for word; the story itself is Joshua 7

translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). The two opening questions quote Joshua 22:20 LXX almost word for word; the story itself is Joshua 7. LXX 'Achar son of Zara' given in the usual English Bible form 'Achan son of Zerah'. ἀνάθεμα rendered 'what was under the ban' / 'a thing under the ban' in both places so that Gregory's application of the word to present gain stays visible. The second question (μὴ μόνος ἀπέθανεν) expects the answer no. πλημμελείᾳ ἐπλημμέλησεν (cognate emphasis) rendered 'commit a grave trespass'.
orientation: Gregory warns that greed at this moment is anathema, drawing on the example of Achan whose single sin brought wrath on all Israel, and contrasts Achan's plunder of enemies with the current plundering of brothers.

title: Restoring lost property as a sacred duty from Deuteronomy and Exodus
english: Let no one deceive himself; for it is not permitted to gain even if one finds something. Deuteronomy says: You must not disregard your brother's ox or sheep wandering on the road; by turning back you shall turn them back to your brother. If your brother is not near you and you do not know him, you shall gather them and they shall stay with you until your brother seeks them out and you shall restore them to him. You shall do the same with his donkey, and you shall do the same with his garment, and you shall do the same for every loss of your brother, whatever he may lose and you find. This is what Deuteronomy says. In Exodus, not only if one finds something of a brother but also of an enemy: by turning back you shall turn them back to the house of their master. If it is not permitted to gain from a brother or an enemy who in time of peace is living carelessly and luxuriating while neglecting his own things, how much more when he is suffering misfortune, fleeing enemies, and by necessity leaving behind his own things?
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, p. 2, Canon δ´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer

added_allusions.reason: Deuteronomy named by Gregory; LXX quoted (μόσχον ... πρόβατον ... ἀποστροφῇ ἀποστρέψεις)
an enemy's stray animal must be returned; Gregory's wording ('to the house of their owner') differs from the LXX as usually printed

translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). The print sets a Greek question mark after ἑαυτόν; the sense is a command and is rendered so. Μηδεὶς ἐξαπατάτω ἑαυτόν has the wording of 1 Corinthians 3:18, but it is a stock phrase and Gregory does not apply Paul's context; possible echo only, not cited. μήτε ὡς εὑρών rendered 'nor plead that he found the goods' ('the goods' supplied for English). Deuteronomy 22:1–3 LXX quoted. The Exodus line is named by Gregory and matches the content of Exodus 23:4 (an enemy's stray animal), but its wording ('to the house of their owner') differs from the LXX text as usually printed (ἀποστρέψας ἀποδώσεις αὐτῷ); cited as Exodus 23:4, English follows Gregory's wording. κυρίου αὐτῶν = their human owner, so lower-case. 'this holds' supplied for the Greek ellipsis. πόσῳ μᾶλλον ('how much more [is it forbidden]') rendered with the English idiom 'how much less'.
orientation: Gregory continues arguing that anyone who found and kept property from the devastated region has stolen from brothers, citing Deuteronomy's law on returning a brother's stray animals and Exodus's extension even to enemies' property.

title: Self-deception with stolen property and sending Euphrosynus to restore church order
english: Others, however, deceive themselves. In place of their own lost property, they hold onto what belongs to others that they have found. They do this so that, since the Boradi and Goths treated them as enemies, they themselves might become Boradi and Goths to other people. Therefore we have sent our brother and fellow-presbyter Euphrosynus to you on account of these matters, so that he too might act according to the pattern here, both accepting the accusations that must be accepted and proclaiming excluded from the prayers those who must be excluded.
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, p. 2, Canon ε´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer
ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). Βοράδοι καὶ Γότθοι = the Boradi and the Goths, the raiders of Pontus. τὰ τῶν πολεμίων εἰργάσαντο rendered 'have dealt with them as enemies'. συγγέρων rendered 'fellow elder' (fellow presbyter). δῴῃ has no expressed object; 'direction' is supplied for English, and the two clauses that follow are what he is to give direction about. Doubtful reading: Vossius' Latin ('ut secundum formam quae hic est, etiam ibi det similiter') suggests his Greek had 'there' (ἐκεῖ) where this print has αὐτός ('he too'); the English follows the print. ἐκκηρῦξαι τῶν εὐχῶν rendered 'shut out of the prayers'. No Scripture.
orientation: Gregory exposes captives who keep looted goods to compensate their own losses, warns they become like the barbarians, and sends the presbyter Euphrosynus so the addressee can apply the same restitution rule and exclude the guilty from the prayers.

title: Report of captives held by force and call for intervention
english: Something unbelievable has been reported to us as having been done in your region — surely by unbelievers, godless people who do not even know the name of the Lord. Some have advanced to such a degree of savagery and inhumanity that they are holding by force certain captives who had escaped. Send some people into the region, lest thunderbolts fall upon those who do such things.
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, p. 2, Canon ς´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer
ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). The play on ἄπιστον / ἀπίστων ('unbelievable' / 'unbelievers') is kept as 'beyond belief' / 'unbelievers'. πάντως που ('surely, I suppose') is ironic: such things could only be expected of unbelievers. χώρα rendered 'district' both times. Κυρίου = the Lord (God), capitalised. σκηπτοί = thunderbolts; not a Scripture citation. Correction βία → βίᾳ follows the source note.
orientation: Gregory reports hearing that some escaped captives are being violently detained in the addressee's region by unbelievers, and urges sending people to intervene before the perpetrators fall into a trap.

title: Treatment of apostate captives who turned against their own people
english: I must address those who were enrolled among the barbarians and went on with them in captivity. They forgot that they were Pontians and Christians, and became thoroughly barbarized — so much so that they even murdered their fellow-tribesmen, whether with a club or by strangling. They also showed the barbarians roads and houses that had been unknown to them. These people must be barred from the hearing until some common decision about them might seem good to the saints assembled together, and before them to the Holy Spirit.

ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
Inline Acts 15:28

added_allusions.reason: ἔδοξε ... τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, the council formula of Acts 15:28 with the order reversed; a clear echo, not a quotation

translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). ἐν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ ἐπελθόντας is ambiguous ('attacked with them in the captivity'); read as Pontic captives who were enlisted and then joined the raiders' attacks, so 'while captives, joined them in their attacks'. ξύλῳ rendered 'with a club'; it could also mean a gallows or stake (ANF 'gibbet'); ἀγχόνη = noose, strangling. ἀκρόασις is the penitential grade of the hearers (see section 11), so 'the stage of hearing'. The closing words echo the council formula of Acts 15:28 (ἔδοξε τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι καὶ ἡμῖν), with the order reversed by 'before them'; cited as a clear allusion, not a quotation; the English keeps 'seems good to … the Holy Spirit' so the echo stays visible. Χριστιανοί printed lower-case in the source; 'Christians' capitalised as English requires. κοινῇ correction follows the source note.
orientation: Gregory instructs the bishop on how to handle captives who defected to the barbarians, committed murder against fellow Christians, and guided the enemy; they must be excluded from the church's hearing pending a joint decision with the saints and the Holy Spirit.

title: Treatment of those who entered strangers' houses during the invasion
english: If you find that those who dared to enter houses not their own have been accused and convicted, you must not even admit them to the rank of hearers. But if they confess themselves and make restitution, they are to be placed in the order of those who are returning.
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, p. 2, Canon η´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer
ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial; it adds 'during the barbarian raid'). ἐπελθεῖν rendered 'raid' (come upon, assail). ἀξιώσῃς is second person singular, addressed to the bishop, hence 'you should not admit them'. ἑαυτοὺς ἐξείπωσι = declare themselves, confess without being charged ('confess on their own'). ἐν τῇ τῶν ὑποστρεφόντων τάξει ὑποπίπτειν as printed: ὑποπίπτειν names the kneeling grade (ὑπόπτωσις, section 11) and ὑποστρέφοντες are 'those who are returning' (the returning penitents; 'turning back' avoided because in English it can suggest falling away); not checked against a second Greek witness. Correction ἐαυτοὺς → ἑαυτοὺς follows the source note. No Scripture.
orientation: Gregory continues his pastoral instructions to the bishop, now addressing a third category of offenders: those who dared enter houses not their own during the barbarian incursion, with different outcomes depending on whether they are convicted or confess.

title: Penance for captives found in fields or own homes
english: But those who found something in the field or in their own houses, left there by the barbarians -- if they are accused and convicted, let them likewise be placed among the prostrators. If, however, they confess and make satisfaction, then deem them worthy of the prayers.
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, p. 2, Canon θ´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer
ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). The clauses are elliptical: the verb for the first ('are to be') is understood from section 8, and ἀξιῶσαι depends on an understood 'one should' (hence 'are to be admitted', not the weaker 'may'). ἐν τοῖς ὑποπίπτουσιν = among the kneelers (penitential grade, section 11); ὁμοίως rendered 'they too' (likewise, as in section 8). τῆς εὐχῆς = the prayer of the faithful, the standing-together grade; καί = 'even'. No corrections; no Scripture.
orientation: Gregory continues his instructions to the bishop about handling captives, now addressing those found in fields or their own houses left by barbarians, setting conditions for their restoration to prayer.

title: Instruction for those fulfilling the commandment without greed
english: Those who carry out the command must fulfill it without any shameful gain, refusing to demand informer fees, seizure rewards, finder's fees, or payments by whatever name these things are called.
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, p. 2, Canon ι´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer
ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial; it spells εὕρητρα, the text εὕρετρα; text kept). τὴν ἐντολήν = the command to return lost property set out in section 4 (Deuteronomy 22:1–3; Exodus 23:4); not cited again here because the canon names no text. αἰσχροκέρδεια rendered 'greed for shameful gain', matching section 2. μήνυτρα, σῶστρα, εὕρετρα = fees for information, for rescue (salvage), for finding.
orientation: Gregory instructs the bishop that those who fulfill the commandment must do so without any form of shameful gain, forbidding demands for informer fees, rewards for seizure, or finder's fees under any name.

title: Penitential stations and the final goal of the mysteries
english: The weeping takes place outside the gate of the prayer house, where the one who has sinned must stand and beg the faithful as they enter to pray for him. The hearing takes place inside the gate in the narthex, where the one who has sinned must stand until the catechumens depart, and from there he must leave, for 'hearing the Scriptures and the teaching, let him be put out and not be deemed worthy of prayer.' The falling prostrate means he stands inside the gate of the sanctuary and leaves with the catechumens. The standing together means he stands with the faithful and does not leave with the catechumens. Last of all comes the sharing of the holy things.
notes_covered: Greek copy-text: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR typed print, pp. 2-3, Canon ια´; read from the page image and matched against its text layer
ANF consulted only as sense check; not copied
translator_notes: Rubric left out (editorial). Usually judged a later addition, not Gregory's own words: Vossius notes it was absent from the Greek Nomocanon and found only in Cardinal Sirleto's manuscript; translated in full as printed. Names of the grades: πρόσκλαυσις 'Weeping', ἀκρόασις 'Hearing', ὑπόπτωσις 'Kneeling' (literally falling down), σύστασις 'Standing together', μέθεξις τῶν ἁγιασμάτων 'sharing in the holy things'. ἕως τῶν κατηχουμένων ('until the catechumens') rendered 'until the catechumens leave' (the dismissal is understood). ναός rendered 'the church itself' (the main hall, as against the narthex). The quoted line (ἀκούων γάρ, φησί …) is not Scripture and its source is unnamed; left uncited. συνίσταται after ἵνα (indicative, late usage) kept and rendered as 'stands with'. Corrections χρἠ → χρὴ and μετᾶ → μετὰ follow the source note.
orientation: Gregory lists the ordered places where a penitent stands — outside the gate of the prayer house, inside the gate in the narthex, within the gate of the temple, admitted to the faithful, and finally sharing in the holy mysteries — marking each stage by where the person stands and whether they leave with the catechumens or stay with the faithful.
